difficulty.note: No public difficulty label found for this arrangement.

readinessReasons: In some places one hand is asked to strike keys too far apart to reach at once (wider than a tenth). Some of those notes may belong to the other hand, or the chord may be meant to be rolled.

overrides.reason: The music for the two hands is written as two separate one-staff parts. The top part is higher than the bottom part in almost every measure, so the top part is played with the right hand and the bottom part with the left hand. In measures 40, 41, 53 and 59 the right-hand melody dips below some left-hand notes: the hands cross there, they are not swapped.
